evidence: Single package ('varken') with one main entry point (Varken.py), indicating one cohesive deployable unit
Domains are well-factored into logically related modules (e.g., per-integration APIs: sonarr.py, radarr.py, tautulli.py) but all in same package and process
Shared infrastructure components (dbmanager, helpers, iniparser, structures) are reused across modules without loose coupling or isolation
No service boundaries or inter-process communication—modules interact via direct imports and function calls
CLI-only execution model with scheduled threads (using 'schedule' library), typical of data aggregation monoliths
Minimal directory depth (max 2) and flat structure, avoiding layered or service-oriented layering
Use of NamedTuples (structures.py) for data exchange within same process, not over network protocols
risks: Risk of tight coupling as domain modules (e.g., radarr.py, tautulli.py) share utilities and structures but have no clear boundary enforcement
Threading model using 'schedule' + Thread suggests potential scalability issues under load
Single-point-of-failure: failure in one integration or the DB manager can halt entire application
Limited testability due to direct imports across modules without abstraction layers
Difficulty scaling or deploying specific integrations independently
